hints.content:
### The strategy

The tangent of an angle in a right triangle is the ratio between the length of the side opposite to that angle and length of the side adjacent to that angle.

So we should pick any expression that matches this description for $\angle R$.

However, we should also consider expressions given in terms of the other acute angle in $\triangle PQR$, angle $\angle Q$, which is the complementary angle of $\angle R$.

[[☃ explanation 1]]

options.showPrompt: Learn about the relationship between trig ratios of complementary angles.

hints.content:
### Using $\angle R$

The tangent of $\angle R$ is the ratio $\dfrac{PQ}{PR}$. We can also describe it as $\dfrac{\text{length of side opposite to }\angle R}{\text{length of side adjacent to }\angle R}$.

### Using $\angle Q$

Now let's think of the complementary $\angle Q$.

The ratio $\dfrac{PQ}{PR}$ is the same as $\dfrac{\text{length of side adjacent to }\angle Q}{\text{length of side opposite to }\angle Q}$. This, in turn, is the same as $\dfrac{1}{\tan(\angle Q)}$.

Notice that this makes sense because the tangent of an angle always equals the reciprocal of the tangent of its complementary angle, and vice versa.

Overall, we found four expressions that are equivalent to $\tan(\angle R)$. Out of those, the following two are options:

- $\dfrac{PQ}{PR}$

- $\dfrac{\text{length of side adjacent to }\angle Q}{\text{length of side opposite to }\angle Q}$
